newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: IAEA chief says nuclear power cuts greenhouse gases.
newsitem.headline: IAEA chief says nuclear power cuts greenhouse gases.

text.p: The director-general of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said on Monday that wider use of nuclear power could help reduce greenhouse gas emissions, which contribute to global warming.

In a speech to the General Assembly, Hans Blix said studies showed that fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas were the main culprits for greenhouse gases, while nuclear power and renewable sources of energy contributed the least amount.

"There should now be a general awareness among governments that an expanded use of nuclear power and of renewable sources of energy together with conservation measures could significantly help to restrain greenhouse gas emissions."

He said some governments -- Japan, South Korea, China and Eastern Europe -- invoked environmental concerns in defending their expanded use of nuclear power. "However, at present most countries are continuing to expand their use of fossil fuels and are failing to meet targets which they have set for themselves to restrain their emissions of greenhouse gases."
He said the IAEA was also dealing with other areas of concern including safety in nuclear power operation and waste disposal and illicit trafficking in nuclear materials.
"Results of the efforts to strengthen nuclear safety can be seen in the reduced number of unplanned stoppages in nuclear power plants around the world," Blix said.

Commenting on non-power uses of nuclear techniques, he cited as an example the use of radiation to sterilise such insects as the Mediterranean fruit fly and the tsetse fly. He said the New World screwworm had been eliminated in Libya a few years ago while a promising project was underway to eradicate the tsetse fly from Zanzibar in Tanzania by the end of 1997, which would improve cattle rearing on the island.
